profile.reading:
CloudHQ LC11 sits at 22235 Loudoun County Parkway, Ashburn, Virginia, one of fourteen numbered buildings on CloudHQ's LC Campus, which the company's own current campus page places directly off Loudoun County Parkway "in the heart of Ashburn," describing the site as sitting amid "the densest concentration of fiber in the world." A third-party data center aggregator separately reports 108 megawatts specifically for LC11, a figure this profile notes as unconfirmed by the operator rather than adopting as fact. CloudHQ states the full LC Campus totals roughly 8.5 million square feet and 1,256 megawatts of total critical IT load across its fourteen data centers, with 756 megawatts currently available, a campus-wide total not broken out by individual building. CloudHQ was founded in 2016 by Hossein Fateh, who also founded QTS Realty Trust and, per CloudHQ's own materials, was the first person in the United States to obtain an IRS ruling allowing data center income to qualify for real estate investment trust tax treatment. CloudHQ is privately held through the Fateh Family Office, with regional headquarters in Washington DC, London, and Singapore, and states a company-wide net-zero emissions target by 2040, along with generator fuel supplied by HVO biodiesel "wherever it is reliably available." CloudHQ does not name a power utility for the LC Campus on its current site; Dominion Energy is the dominant electric utility across Loudoun County as a matter of public record.

Loudoun County's Ashburn corridor is the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world, hosting dozens of competing hyperscale and colocation operators within a few miles of CloudHQ's LC Campus. CloudHQ's global portfolio spans 23 campuses and more than 30 million square feet across six countries, with more than 1,380 megawatts of critical IT load already contracted company-wide and over 6,000 megawatts of further expansion potential, figures CloudHQ discloses on its own homepage alongside a stated 5.2-gigawatt global data center inventory.

reading.body:
CloudHQ LC11 is one of fourteen buildings on the LC Campus in Ashburn, Virginia, located directly off Loudoun County Parkway in what the operator describes as the heart of the world's densest fiber concentration. The campus as a whole publishes 1,256 megawatts of total critical IT load across 8.5 million square feet, with 756 megawatts currently available for lease, though this figure is not broken down by individual building. A third-party aggregator reports 108 megawatts for LC11 specifically, unconfirmed by CloudHQ's published materials.

Ashburn's data center corridor hosts dozens of competing hyperscale and colocation operators within a few miles of this site, making location the primary competitive asset rather than uniqueness. The LC Campus sits in Virginia's largest published data center concentration, which totals 1,375 megawatts across 23 facilities with published figures out of 330 mapped data centers statewide. At the campus level, CloudHQ's 756 megawatts of available capacity represents a meaningful share of Virginia's published inventory, though the operator does not publish per-building specifications.

The power utility serving this site is not published by CloudHQ; Dominion Energy is the dominant utility across Loudoun County as public record. Whether CloudHQ LC11 matters to AI scaling depends on securing lease commitments from the 756 megawatts of available capacity across the full campus, which requires access to Virginia's electrical grid within the binding constraints that now govern data center expansion in this region.
